findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ('*'), violating least privilege and allowing this IAM user to perform virtually any operation on these services, including data exfiltration, resource destruction, and privilege escalation.

A long-lived programmatic access key is created for the IAM user instead of using temporary credentials or role assumption. Combined with the excessively permissive policy attached to this user, leakage of this key would grant an attacker broad, non-expiring access to the account.

findings.issue_category: standalone IAM user with excessive privileges
findings.description: An individual IAM user is created and directly attached to an overly permissive policy rather than using role-based access with temporary credentials, increasing blast radius if the associated access key is compromised.

The IAM access key's encrypted secret is exposed via a Terraform output; even though it is the KMS/PGP-encrypted value rather than raw plaintext, exposing key material through outputs risks it being persisted in the Terraform state file and shown in CLI/log output, increasing the chance of credential leakage.
